items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I got asked to join the Dorsey band that night by the leader, Buddy Morrow... I was on that band for about two and a half years.

ctx.x: How did — your first big job, that you said man, I’ve been working towards this and this finally happened.

It’s kind of a two part thing. When I was living in Cleveland and I was playing of course in this polka band, and at the same time I started branching out and playing with jazz groups around town. Flash forward a few years, I’m in college. I get called to play at a jazz festival in Cleveland with my own group, and it’s me, the Teddy Wilson trio and the Tommy Dorsey band — a ghost band — but so anyway so I do this concert and it’s a big deal for me. And I got asked to join the Dorsey band that night by the leader,…

items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: That’s the one he did for me, but I did one for him called “Lazy Afternoon.”

ctx.x: Yes I do. There’s an American Express one that I did that’s played a lot, and Applebee’s, which is a chain, I’m on those. That’s kind of a fun thing. It’s fun to hear myself on the radio once in a while too, on a jazz station. And actually I really honestly, I’m not trying to be falsely modest or anything, but I just don’t listen to my own records. It’s like watching home movies for me. It’s like it’s done, time to move on to the next thing, and I hear every mistake and everything I’d want to fix. And when I do…
That’s the one he did for me, but I did one for him called “Lazy Afternoon.”
